key_insight: The paper shows that spiking neural networks can be redesigned together with specialized hardware to use much less memory and compute without sacrificing performance. A dual memory pathway architecture, matched to a custom neuromorphic chip, achieves over 4× higher throughput and 5× better energy efficiency.
problem_solved: Neuromorphic and spiking AI systems often struggle to balance accuracy, parameter count, speed, and energy use on real hardware. This work addresses the gap between algorithm design and chip architecture by co-optimizing both for efficient deployment.
method: Designs a spiking neural network with two memory pathways to improve efficiency and hardware compatibility.
Co-designs the network architecture with a custom neuromorphic chip so computation and memory access are better aligned.
Reduces model size by 40–60% while improving throughput and energy efficiency compared with state-of-the-art implementations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a practical path to building faster and more energy-efficient edge or embedded AI systems. It highlights that algorithm-hardware co-design can deliver substantial gains beyond software-only optimization.
